title: Reliable, Smart Workflows for Finance, Wealth and Insurance — Karthic Rao, Perpetual
talk_summary: Karthic Rao describes Perpetual's workflow engine for regulated wealth management, where a deterministic compiler turns an LLM-produced semantic graph into an immutable, hash-pinned execution plan, and LLM calls are confined to small typed judgment steps. The core claim is that ~95% of decisions can run on a small/flash model (or locally hosted), with only genuinely hard cases going to a frontier model, and every judgment is logged and human-confirmed to become training data.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic control flow with LLM only at judgment points
takeaways.what_they_do: A planner LLM translates a request into a typed semantic graph; a deterministic compiler (no model calls) validates it against a fixed action grammar and emits an immutable, hash-pinned plan; a state machine executes it, calling the model only for small typed judgments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: El determinismo gobierna el flujo de control, la evidencia y los efectos secundarios... La inteligencia proporciona interpretación y juicio.
takeaways.numbers: ~95% of decisions routed to flash-level model; 19 of 20 illustrative decisions on flash, 1 on frontier

takeaways.technique: Typed small-model judgments, frontier only for hard cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Every judgment call has a fixed schema and is small (classify, extract, match, completeness check), so a fast small model handles it; only genuinely hard cases escalate to a frontier model, and the frontier share shrinks over releases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: cerca del 95%de las decisiones no necesiten un modelo de frontera... Solo los casos genuinamente difíciles van a un modelo de frontera.

takeaways.technique: Human-confirmed judgments become labeled training/eval data
takeaways.what_they_do: Provisional model judgments stay blocked until a human confirms or rejects them; each confirmed judgment is logged with its typed schema, producing graded eval data that can post-train the small model and reduce frontier quota over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Cada decisión de frontera produce por construcción datos de entrenamiento reales con calificación de evaluación.

takeaways.technique: Action grammar + approval gates bound to payload hash
takeaways.what_they_do: The compiler only accepts actions in a closed grammar of ~42 typed contracts; external side effects (send, submit, sign) each require human approval bound to the exact payload hash and re-verified just before execution; no automatic retries, unknown outcomes go to manual review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: La aprobación está vinculada al hash del payload exacto y se verifica de nuevo justo antes de enviar.

takeaways.technique: Waits, approvals, and follow-ups as plan nodes, not prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Long human-latency steps (wait for response, approval, follow-up) are explicit state-machine nodes with timeouts (default 72h, 1min–30d) and deterministic expiry rules; follow-ups spawn child plans capped at 5 rounds while the parent plan stays immutable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Una espera de respuesta tiene un valor predeterminado de 72 horas... Cuando expira, una regla decide qué sucede, no un modelo.
takeaways.numbers: 72h default wait; 1min–30d range; max 5 follow-up rounds

takeaways.technique: Small typed calls instead of one big agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Each model call is a narrow, schema-verified judgment (is this complete, does this match, which field is this), so context stays small and the same call can be repointed to a private/local model by changing one config line.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Cada llamada al modelo es pequeña, tipada y verificada contra un esquema... apuntar a un modelo alojado de forma privada es un cambio de configuración, no una reescritura.
